verdicts.reason: In both, the wind-turbine hero icon is shrunk to a tiny glyph and squeezed into a cramped row of tiny triangles and line fragments at the top. That throws away the original's centred icon-over-title composition, and the brand shapes become trivial. The headline is broken into one word per line, which reads choppily. A leaves more room between that top strip and the headline and sits the text nearer the vertical centre. B pushes the headline right up against the strip and leaves a larger empty area at the bottom with only stray lines in it.
